spec.title: Central stewardship of a long campaign

p.CENTRAL-JOB: The central coordinator owns the coherent idea: reconstructing the mandate, architecture, dependencies and risks; maintaining the lossless plan; choosing atoms; reviewing actual output; issuing acceptance; promoting knowledge; integrating commits; and proving closure. Tools and workers may execute bounded work, but these judgments remain central even when delegation is cheap.

p.ACTIVITY-NOT-PROGRESS: Tool calls, generated code, green producer tests, commits and completed UI rows are activity. Progress is an obligation moving to a justified disposition with durable evidence while the remaining route stays truthful.

p.EXECUTION-AUTHORITY: First resolve the current owner instruction: inspection/status, planning, or execution. A stored next atom, generated goal, ready node or available worker does not authorize starting implementation. Preserve explicit holds and stops. Within authorized execution, routine continuation, recovery and bounded retries need no repeated permission; a new action outside that authority does.

facts.LOOP-ORIENT: **Orient:** on cold start, ordinary resume, compaction with lost plan context, or context change, read authority and the complete plan; verify the exact binding, tree, selected campaign goal, candidates and accepted boundary. During a continuous warm run, reuse that complete model only while the plan revision and captured input identity still match; read every known change before relying on it. Unknown changes or incomplete memory require a complete reread. Treat ordinary custody metadata as advisory. Refresh a stale `GOAL.md` in an owner-facing continuation unless a formal handoff is currently `offering`.
facts.LOOP-REFINE: **Refine:** expand one coherent frontier region around the next meaningful accepted outcome, using existing stable node ids. Judge viable existing candidates before opening more work. State dependencies, write perimeter, acceptance, essential verification and safe stop; apply `DISPATCH-READINESS` before execution. Add a mutation diagnostic only after the suspicion and economy conditions in `MUTATION-DIAGNOSTIC-LAW` are met.
facts.LOOP-EXECUTE: **Execute:** work directly or commission bounded workers according to the project's delegation policy. Preserve ordinary inspectable artifacts.
facts.LOOP-JUDGE: **Judge:** inspect the real diff/result against architecture and mandate, reproduce decisive essential gates under `VERIFICATION-SUBJECT`, and inspect for concrete false-green signals. Judge each candidate centrally; additional independent review is chosen for consequential uncertainty, not repeated merely because the session or producer changed. If suspicious, apply `MUTATION-DIAGNOSTIC-LAW`; do not mutate by ritual.
facts.LOOP-INTEGRATE: **Integrate:** repair or reject defects; promote stable discoveries; commit atomically; update acceptance tier, dependencies and projection.
facts.LOOP-LOOK-BACK: **Look back:** ask what the result falsified, what new obligation appeared, what knowledge still lives only in a report, and whether distant architecture still composes. Re-evaluate the route and actual dependencies unlocked; replan where evidence requires it before selecting the next atom. This need not rewrite an unchanged plan after every step. Milestone and closure backscans remain mandatory.

p.LOOP-NOT-AUTOMATION: This is an operating discipline, not an automatic product loop. Human intervention, long-running creative work and indeterminate iteration are normal. Lifecycle systems may provide evidence and phase mechanics without choosing the next action.

p.WORKING-OUTCOME: A working window names the behavior, invariant, usable interface or recoverable operation its existing nodes should establish. It is a bounded view of the complete plan, not another queue or replacement schema. Prefer admissible work that unlocks an important dependency, resolves costly uncertainty or exposes integration risk early; compare verification cost and available resources. Explain the decisive reason briefly. Do not invent precision with weighted scores, rank by descendant count, or equate a small task count with a useful result. Use declared ordering and stable ids to break otherwise equivalent choices.

p.DISPATCH-READINESS: Before dispatch, verify that required prerequisites have their declared acceptance tier, actual inputs and interfaces are available, the write perimeter includes necessary registration/integration files, and observable acceptance has named essential checks. Distinguish commands that exist now from checks the atom must implement. Name their expected behavior, the safe stop and recovery route; confirm needed resources and current authority. Missing information becomes bounded preparation or refinement of the affected existing nodes. It does not authorize a worker to invent architecture, skip a dependency or restart the entire campaign.

p.INPUT-CHANGE: Expected writes by the current coordinator or its known disjoint workers require recapturing affected inputs and invalidating dependent evidence, not asking for the same authority again. An observed conflicting live writer or unexplained semantic change stops affected writes for resolution; preserve independent safe work. A changed timestamp or stale custody claim alone does not prove a conflict.

p.REASON-FROM-MODEL: Do not reduce a large campaign to the number of rows a harness happens to display. Reconstruct the hierarchy from mandate and evidence, keep unresolved uncertainty explicit, and reason across phase boundaries before local optimization. When a change affects the core idea, update the route first, not retrospectively.

p.ULTRA-DISCIPLINE: Under `ultra`, use the available extended reasoning to keep architecture, distant dependencies and acceptance in one coherent model. Larger atoms are allowed only where their result remains reviewable. Deep reasoning is not permission to leave conclusions only in context or skip mechanical proof.

p.STANDARD-DISCIPLINE: Under `standard`, externalize more of the decision structure before acting: smaller atoms, explicit claim-to-evidence mappings, frequent backscans and stronger preference for independent review. Persist concise conclusions, assumptions and next checks, not a transcript of private reasoning. Never compensate for limited context by silently dropping distant stages or declaring a shallow plan complete.

workers.title: 4. Workers are producers, never custody shortcuts

p.WORKER-PACKET: When workers are used, one packet has a bounded goal, closed write perimeter, supplied architecture, acceptance and exact self-checks, plus a durable report location. The worker returns ordinary inspectable files and evidence; it does not commit, hide state inside a private representation, claim central review or advance project status unless project policy explicitly makes it a central session instead. Supply only the standing rules, permanent anchors, accepted prerequisite outputs, relevant interfaces, current delta and known pitfalls needed for this packet. Name them explicitly; do not dump the complete campaign or require every worker to rediscover its context. A missing governing input is a packet defect to report, not permission to silently widen scope.

p.WORKER-REVIEW: Review a worker result like an untrusted but capable pull request: compare the actual artifact to the packet, verify every consequential claim, and inspect whether its tests exercise and assert the claimed behavior. Use a counterfactual mutation only under `MUTATION-DIAGNOSTIC-LAW`. A worker's PASS, token count or confident narrative cannot substitute for acceptance.

p.WORKER-FAILURE: A transport error, timeout or killed final turn is not a code verdict. Inspect what survived, preserve it, then recalculate whether the remainder is cheaper to repair centrally, resume, recommission or reject. Never delete first or restart blindly. Follow [`interruption-recovery.xml`](interruption-recovery.xml) for provider failures, quota exhaustion, interrupted effects and ordinary continuation.

p.PARALLEL-WORK: Parallelize independent work only after shared contracts are settled and write perimeters, shared resources and integration order are compatible. Name one integration owner. Size the active window to available review and integration capacity: if viable candidates accumulate, judge and integrate them before adding producers. Completion order is not dependency order. Do not duplicate a worker whose job may still be live, and do not lower acceptance because a cheaper model produced the result.

p.EXACT-GATES: Every atom runs formatting, diff hygiene and exact affected tests/checks/lints as applicable to its change, including applicable ordinary negative-case and invariant tests. Those tests are essential verification, not counterfactual mutation. A pipe or wrapper that discards the child exit status is telemetry, not a gate.

p.VERIFICATION-SUBJECT: Evidence names the claim and the actual subject checked: relevant source/input bytes, dependencies, fixtures, schemas, configuration, command and flags, toolchain, target and any consequential environment. Reuse existing evidence only when that complete subject still matches and the claim is covered. A commit id alone cannot prove an unchanged environment or dependency closure. If closure is unknown, rerun the affected gate. Preserve accepted history; a new session, account, model or producer alone does not invalidate evidence or require reaccepting unchanged work. Changed subjects and previously unaccepted candidates still need the applicable review and checks.

p.SHARED-GATE-RUN: One stable integration run may establish evidence for several nodes when it actually executes their required cases and retains a claim-to-result mapping for each. Do not substitute a broad green exit for omitted cases, delay a prerequisite gate until after its dependent action, or silently remove an explicit required command. Consolidate duplicate invocations on the same subject; do not consolidate away obligations. Broaden or repeat checks when changes, failures, unknown coverage or integration boundaries justify it, not to fill an activity quota.

p.FULL-PANEL-TRIGGERS: An expensive full panel belongs at a coherent integration boundary, after broad shared-foundation change, before release/publication, or at final campaign acceptance. Do not run it reflexively after every small atom; do not omit it merely because every atom had local tests. The panel is the declared integration/release gate for the affected subject: publishing one leaf package does not select the entire host product or an unstarted campaign's suite. Name that scope and its required checks. The panel must run on the unchanged tree being accepted.

p.MUTATION-DIAGNOSTIC-LAW: **Counterfactual mutation is suspicion-triggered diagnostic evidence, never an atom ritual.** Essential verification always runs first. A mutation may run only when both a concrete observed signal makes the result or test suspicious and the smallest targeted mutation is cheaper than the best named alternative proof. Suspicious signals include: changed behavior that changes no relevant assertion or output; an affected path that is skipped, swallowed or replaced by a mock; an assertion that accepts empty data, an over-broad match or the wrong object; a wrapper that loses exit status or a target test that was not selected; a test coupled to implementation structure without an independent oracle; contradiction with a specification, direct reproduction, trace, snapshot, golden or other independent check; and a pass that is flaky or cannot be reproduced on the acceptance tree. Public or safety-critical surface and worker-produced code raise scrutiny but are not suspicious by themselves. When no concrete signal exists, run no mutation and do not launch a separate investigation merely to justify that absence. Before mutation, record one hypothesis, the smallest reversible edit, one exact affected command, the expected red result and why this is cheaper than the named alternative. The default budget is one mutation and one exact rerun; one replacement mutation is allowed only when the first could not execute, never merely because its result was inconvenient or ambiguous. The episode is this suspicion on this input subject; record consumed attempts with its ordinary evidence. Restart, context loss, worker replacement or account change does not renew that budget. If its consumed budget cannot be reconstructed, treat the diagnostic allowance as spent and use the named alternative; uncertainty does not authorize another mutant. Stop after the observation. Red shows sensitivity only if the selected behavioral assertion fails for the predicted reason; compilation/setup failure or zero selected tests is unusable, not a killed mutant. A green survivor is not automatically a defective test: first adjudicate whether the edit changed behavior within the contract and reached the asserted path. An equivalent or out-of-contract edit is inconclusive; an unexpectedly unexercised required path or false-green oracle is a defect to repair. If inconclusive or no longer economical, use the named alternative or replan without searching for more mutants. Restore the original bytes and reproduce essential gates on the restored acceptance subject before acceptance. Open-ended mutant search, mutation-score chasing and whole-suite mutation loops are forbidden unless the owner separately authorizes a diagnostic campaign with its own budget and exit criteria.

p.MUTATION-POLICY-DECISION: **Decision:** counterfactual mutation is a bounded, suspicion-triggered diagnostic, not a routine acceptance gate. **Why:** full mutation work consumes disproportionate tokens and can trap an agent in repeated mutant attempts for days while exact affected checks usually supply the needed evidence. **Considered and rejected:** mutation at every atom or public boundary is predictably too expensive; banning all mutation discards a useful probe when a pass is concretely suspicious. **When to revisit:** repeated false-green defects escape essential verification, or the owner explicitly commissions a dedicated mutation-quality campaign with a measured budget.

p.TEST-THE-TEST: Inspect test relevance and sensitivity, especially at public boundaries, for safety properties and around easily vacuous assertions. Those risk categories increase scrutiny but do not themselves trigger mutation. When a concrete suspicious signal exists, follow `MUTATION-DIAGNOSTIC-LAW`; otherwise essential verification is the gate.

p.WISDOM-TRIGGER: At review, milestone and handoff, ask which observations generalize beyond the current atom. Promote a verified product law into its spec, an executable invariant into a test, an operational campaign lesson into the governing flow, and unresolved future work into a named backlog/plan node. Do not wait for session end, when causal context has already decayed.

p.REPORT-RETENTION: A report may be removed only after its unique code is integrated/rejected and every accepted durable fact has another governing home. “The worker finished” and “its knowledge is preserved” are different claims.

p.MEASURE-OUTCOMES: Assess the procedure by accepted behaviors and invariants, exercised recovery scenarios, rework and the backlog of unjudged candidates. When useful, distinguish time spent preparing context, producing work, reviewing and verifying to find the actual bottleneck. Use ordinary evidence, not a mandatory telemetry service. Token counts and completed rows may explain cost; they cannot stand in for quality or useful progress.

p.SAFE-STOP: A safe stop has an internally consistent tree, an explicit accepted boundary, every incomplete artifact classified candidate, a current complete plan, and a literal next recipe. It may occur between atoms even when the campaign is far from complete. A sudden failure may prevent reaching this state; recovery reconstructs the facts and reports the gap rather than claiming the stop was safe.

p.NO-CREATIVE-STOP: Do not transform “hard,” “long,” “resources low,” “worker stopped,” or “visible plan ended” into a creative claim of completion. Continue, preserve recoverable state, or report the real blocker. A formal handoff is used only on explicit owner request. Completion is reserved for proven exit criteria.
